clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old Middle Eastern female presented with a one-month history of excessive cough, mild dyspnea, and left-sided chest pain. Initial chest X-ray showed a 10cm x 8cm opacity in the left lower lobe. Chest CT revealed a hypodense simple pulmonary cyst. Post-surgical pathology of aspirated cyst fluid confirmed Echinococcus infection based on clinical history and microscopic findings, despite similarities with other Taeniidae family hooklets. The patient was treated with Albendazole and discharged with a 10-year follow-up plan.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Chest X-ray revealed a 10cm x 8cm opacity in the left lower lobe.
Chest CT scan showed a hypodense abnormality characteristic of a simple pulmonary cyst.
Post-surgical pathology of cyst fluid was determined to be Echinococcus given the clinical history despite similarity in hooklets to other Taeniidae family members.
Patient was discharged with Albendazole treatment and scheduled serial follow-up chest X-rays.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: No history of tuberculosis contact or typical constitutional symptoms; no imaging features suggestive of TB.
Pathology specifically concluded Echinococcus based on clinical and microscopic correlation.
